text:
Jacob Fowler is the main reason Montreal has 28 points from 20 games. The 2023 third-round pick out of Boston College is 9-1-2 with a .926 save percentage, and he's saved 13.5 more goals than the shots he's faced usually allow, and he ranks second among the league's goalies in wins added by our count. A Winning Habit has already written about him positioning himself for hockey history.

The best part of his game is where it matters most. He's stopping .800 of high-danger shots against a league average of .685, and his medium-danger work is even more valuable, 7.5 goals saved above expected on those alone. He's 3-0-2 over his last five starts with 3.6 saved above expected, and Evolving-Hockey had him well above average in his 17 games last season too.

There are two cautions. Rebounds: 14.5% of his saves lead to another shot within three seconds, against a league 10.8%, which is the kind of thing that catches up with a goalie. And our talent range expects regression, putting his true save rate closer to .890 than .926. He's very good. He's probably not this good every night, and Montreal's results lean on him more than any team should lean on a second-year goalie.
